$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for @platos/kernel's WIN-260 (M2.5) additions: the
transaction-outcome contract in src/ports/unit-of-work.ts and the bounded
retry policy in src/vo/retry.ts. One entry per invariant, each carrying the
file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements it (`from`), the edit that
removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
A guard nothing can turn red is a guard that is not there.
THE KERNEL HAD NO LEDGER BEFORE THIS. Its three original suites cover value
objects whose guards are their own assertions; the two modules added here
are the first kernel code with BEHAVIOUR — a rollback and a bound — and
behaviour is what a mutation ledger is for.
K15–K17 GUARD A TYPE, WHICH IS THE HARDEST KIND OF GUARD TO KEEP. `run`'s
signature refuses a `Result`-valued callback, and `tsc` enforces it on every
build — but if the refusal were dropped, NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY WOULD GO
RED. The tree would compile again and every suite would stay green, because a
type that has stopped refusing looks exactly like a type that had nothing to
refuse. So the three sweep `scripts/arch/transaction-outcome.mjs`, which
compiles probes against the committed port and asserts what the compiler
answered. K17 mutates the GATE rather than the port, and its file is under
scripts/ for that reason: all three guard one invariant and one invariant
belongs in one ledger.
This lives here rather than in README.md because that file is emitted by
scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.mjs and byte-compared by `node
scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.mjs --check`.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. An earlier tranche reported 22 kills and every
one was VACUOUS: the package's dist/ had been cleaned, so every suite failed
to LOAD and would have 'died' against no mutation at all. The driver runs
each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep unless it is green, and
classifies a module-load failure with no named failing case as VACUOUS.
For one entry: replace its `from` with its `to` in the named file, run
`pnpm --filter @platos/kernel exec vitest run <suites>`, and confirm a NAMED
case goes red. Then revert and confirm green.
K01 IS SWEPT TWICE, and the second sweep is the one that matters. The
kernel's own suite drives `runResult` against a double this dimension wrote.
`packages/contexts/cost-monitoring/application/detect-crossings.test.ts`
drives it through a use case, against a double an EARLIER tranche wrote, in
a suite this dimension did not touch — so the second kill is by a case this
dimension does not control. It needs `pnpm --filter @platos/kernel exec tsc
-b` between the mutation and the run, because a context resolves the kernel
through dist/ and a sweep without the rebuild would be vacuous in the other
direction: green against a mutation that never reached the code.
K15–K17 ARE SWEPT AGAINST `node --test
scripts/arch/transaction-outcome.test.mjs` FROM THE REPOSITORY ROOT, not
against a package's vitest. They need NO rebuild: the gate reads
packages/kernel/src/ports/unit-of-work.ts from disk and compiles it, so the
mutation is seen without dist/ being touched — which is also why a sweep of
them cannot be vacuous in the direction the kernel's other entries have to
guard against.

mutations.note: THIS IS THE ONE-CHARACTER-CLASS DIFF THAT PUTS THE DEFECT BACK. Under it the whole tree still compiles and all 1,690-odd suites still pass, because every migrated call site now spells `runResult` and would keep working; what returns is the ABILITY to write `return err(...)` inside `run` and have it COMMIT. Nothing but this gate notices.

mutations.to: export type NotResult<Value> = Value extends unknown ? never : Value;
kills: X1 — the committed port ACCEPTS every shape that is not a Result

mutations.note: THE OTHER DIRECTION, AND IT IS NOT PADDING. A gate that pinned only the refusal would pass happily here — a port that refuses EVERYTHING refuses a Result too. The six accepting probes (void, undefined, a record-or-null union, an array, an ordinary record, and a value read off the transaction scope) are what make the discrimination exact, and they are what would otherwise let a too-wide refusal push honest callbacks back towards the bespoke carriers this dimension removed.

mutations.note: X1 AND X2 ARE TWO CODES BECAUSE THEY ARE TWO FAILURES. X1 says the type has stopped meaning anything; X2 says it still means something and one call site wrote `(unitOfWork as Loose).run(...)` to get past it. This mutation leaves X1 green, which is the proof the two are told apart — the mistake two earlier guards in `privacy` and `identity-access` made by minting one code for both.
